pageIntro: This page explains how we keep you safe, what your rights are and where our transparency documents are. The first section is for everyone; the technical resources at the bottom are for developers and auditors. No personal data; resources that need repository or admin access are marked next to the link.

supplyChain.title: Supply chain (software components used)
supplyChain.sbom: <sbom>SBOM</sbom> (CycloneDX) — the CI workflow that produces it
supplyChain.sbomNote: An SBOM is the list of all open-source packages the application uses. It is not served by the application; it is produced on every main-branch run as the sbom-cyclonedx artifact of the "Security" CI workflow. To download it, open the workflow's latest successful run and take it from the Artifacts section.
supplyChain.provenanceNote: Provenance is a record of which source code and which build steps produced the released build. It is generated by the same workflow and kept in the same run's Artifacts section as the SBOM.
supplyChain.scorecardNote: A tool that automatically scores the security practices of open-source projects. The repository is currently private and Scorecard only publishes scores for public repositories; the workflow is ready and results will be published automatically once the repository is public.

apis.title: Verification endpoints (API)
apis.jwksNote: Public keys needed to check the platform's digital signatures. Third parties use these ES256 keys to verify mandates given to AI agents and signed tokens. The private key is never published.
apis.openapiNote: Machine-readable description of the platform API. It lists all public and authenticated endpoints; agents and integrations use it for discovery.

policies.title: Policies and transparency
policies.securityNote: If you find a security vulnerability, report it through GitHub private security advisories instead of a public issue; first response target is 5 business days.
policies.transparencyNote: Shows notice, removal and appeal counts (no personal data). For now the report is exported as JSON/CSV from the compliance dashboard, which only admins can open.

footnote: Portfolio/demo project; links point to the real workflows and endpoints in the source repository.

rights.title: Your safety and rights
rights.reportNote: If you see a fake or illegal listing or content, tell us. A staff member reviews your notice and the decision with its reasons is sent to your email (EU Digital Services Act, DSA).
rights.appealNote: If you disagree with a moderation decision about your listing or content, appeal with the link in the decision email. An authorised staff member reviews your appeal and the outcome is emailed to you.
rights.rankingNote: Explains which criteria and weights decide the order of search results.
rights.privacyNote: Explains which personal data we process and why, how long we keep it and how to use your rights.
rights.paymentNote: Your card number is not stored on the platform; payments are processed by the payment provider and only a token and the transaction reference are kept.

developers.title: For developers and auditors
developers.intro: The technical resources below are for software developers and security auditors; you do not need them to use the platform.

glossary.sbom: Software Bill of Materials: a list of software components
glossary.slsa: Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts: a software supply-chain security framework
glossary.jwks: JSON Web Key Set: public keys published for verifying signatures
